name: Executive chief-of-staff system
mechanism: Controls or coordinates briefings, senior staff workflow, meeting access, information routing and implementation follow-through around an elected executive.
evidenceFor: Formal White House titles and reporting lines
evidenceAgainst: The President remains the constitutional executive
Agencies, Congress and courts retain independent authority
boundary: This is a documented access system, not proof of a shadow presidency.

name: CPC Central Committee General Office
mechanism: Coordinates central leadership workflow, documents, schedules, communications and implementation channels inside the Chinese Party-state.
evidenceFor: Repeated presence in Xi's top-level state and party activity
evidenceAgainst: The office operates inside collective Party institutions
State Council, military and provincial systems retain distinct functions
boundary: Administrative centrality does not establish a separate hereditary or private sovereign.

name: Russian Presidential Executive Office
mechanism: Supports presidential decision-making, prepares and monitors executive action, coordinates staff and connects the presidency with government, regions and security bodies.
evidenceFor: Documented Security Council and State Council links
evidenceAgainst: Authority is delegated by the President
Ministries and security agencies retain separate chains of command
boundary: A durable executive office can preserve continuity without being an independent hidden government.

name: National-security councils and classified coordination
mechanism: Bring together executive, military, intelligence, diplomatic and economic principals, control sensitive attendance and integrate classified information into decisions.
evidenceFor: Formal national-security adviser and council roles
evidenceAgainst: The councils are attached to constitutional or state executives
Oversight, budgets and agency command remain distributed
boundary: Secrecy is operationally real, but secrecy alone is not evidence of unlawful or unified global command.

name: European Commission Cabinet and Secretariat-General
mechanism: Turns presidential political priorities into coordinated files, manages interinstitutional strategy, senior personnel issues and administrative coherence across the Commission.
evidenceFor: Published responsibilities of the President's Cabinet and Secretariat-General
evidenceAgainst: The College, Council, Parliament, courts and member states share authority
boundary: A policy pipeline can shape timing and content while remaining within a plural legal system.

name: Central-bank executive boards and monetary committees
mechanism: Prepare meetings, control analytical inputs, implement collective decisions and manage day-to-day monetary institutions.
evidenceFor: Statutory committee and Executive Board responsibilities
evidenceAgainst: Votes are collective and mandates are legal
Fiscal policy and elected government remain separate
boundary: Preparation and implementation are powerful; they are not personal ownership of money.

name: Sovereign-fund boards and investment committees
mechanism: Translate state strategy into capital allocation through boards, governors, CEOs, investment committees and delegated authorities.
evidenceFor: Published governance structures and strategy approvals
evidenceAgainst: Portfolio companies and counterparties retain independent governance
Funds remain constrained by mandate, markets and law
boundary: Sovereign capital creates influence and access, not automatic command of recipients or foreign governments.

name: Institutional-capital operating and information platforms
mechanism: Large asset managers combine client relationships, risk systems, operating technology, research and executive networks across markets and institutions.
evidenceFor: Published executive roles and platform responsibilities
Disclosed government, institutional and infrastructure relationships
evidenceAgainst: Managed assets belong to clients and funds
Regulators, boards and contracts constrain action
boundary: Scale and information centrality are not personal ownership or a vote-sharing global council.

name: Dynastic holding, foundation and family-office continuity
mechanism: Preserves voting blocs, board appointment capacity, networks and succession across generations through legal vehicles and family governance.
evidenceFor: Voting disclosures, foundation ownership and current family board roles
evidenceAgainst: Reach is usually company- or sector-specific
Public law, independent boards and minority shareholders remain constraints
boundary: Dynastic continuity is real where enforceable rights exist; it does not verify a unified bloodline government.
